messages.text:
Hi Sarah

Thx for responding.

Please see attached photo of the PSU connectors.  The exposed power cable connections are not UK electrical regulations compliant - the cable is double insulated and should not be exposed in this way.

The PSU supplied with the BitAxe Gamma 602’s I purchased from you - the 50W MeanWell, had the correct termination as they had the IEC-C13 socket.

The PSU fans are absolutely consistent - every 10 mins they run at what sounds like max RPM for 5 mins - this doesn’t sound like normal temp regulation, more likely a faulty PSU or sensor.  Doesn’t matter what temp the room is they run like this consistently.

Let me know what’s to happen. Perhaps replacement PSU with the IEC-C13 socket.

Tx for the $25 code.

Regards

Sent F. My IPhone
Handed to the team · Part needs to be shipped to the customer (UK IEC-C13 terminal cover for LRS-350-

Hi Simon,

Thanks for the photo, that settles it. Your unit went out without its terminal cover, so the mains screw terminals are sitting exposed. That is not how it should have left us, and you are right not to run it like that.

A colleague is picking this up today to get the covered terminal end with the IEC-C13 socket sent out to you, the same style as the one on your Gamma supplies. They will confirm the despatch directly in this thread, and there is nothing for you to send back.

On the fan, our hardware side has gone through it and it is not a fault in the unit. On this Mean Well the fan steps with load rather than room temperature, which is why the open window makes no difference to the cycle you are hearing. If you want to dig into it further with JD, who looks after the hardware, he is quickest on our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, posting in the server and mentioning @nullhashrate.

On flashing the alternate OS, yes, there is a rollback to the shipped image, and JD can walk you through it on the same channel.

Sorry again for how long this took.

Sarah, HeliumDeploy Support
